hooks.text: A single day on Mercury outlasts two of its entire years.
Why does one day on Mercury last two whole planetary years?
176 Earth days pass between a single sunrise and sunset on Mercury.

title: The Planet Where One Day Lasts Two Years
description: For nearly a century, astronomers believed Mercury permanently kept one face to the Sun. Radar observations proved it actually rotates three times for every two orbits.

beats.text: A single day on Mercury outlasts two of its entire years.
beats.visual: Enhanced color global mosaic of Mercury, MESSENGER spacecraft, 2013

beats.text: Astronomers long believed the planet was tidally locked, matching an 88-day orbit with an 88-day spin.
beats.visual: Telescopic view of Mercury in crescent phase from Earth, 1934

beats.text: Under that permanent lock, one roasted hemisphere reached extreme temperatures exceeding 700 Kelvin.
beats.visual: Thermal map showing high surface temperatures across Mercury, MESSENGER, 2011

beats.text: In 1965, scientists bounced radar beams off Mercury to measure its actual spin rate from Earth.
beats.visual: Aerial view of Arecibo Observatory planetary radar dish in Puerto Rico, 1965

beats.text: Italian celestial mechanics specialist Giuseppe Colombo proposed the planet actually rotates once every 59 Earth days.
beats.visual: Portrait of Italian mathematician and celestial mechanics specialist Giuseppe Colombo, 1970

beats.text: Mercury is not locked 1-to-1, but instead rotates three times for every two orbits around the Sun.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating Mercury's 3 to 2 spin-orbit resonance around the Sun, 2008
queries: Mercury 3 to 2 spin orbit resonance diagram

beats.text: Because orbital motion combines with that spin, a single solar day lasts approximately 176 Earth days.
beats.visual: Global view of Mercury's Caloris Basin impact structure, MESSENGER, 2012

beats.text: Every morning there takes two full planetary years to arrive.
beats.visual: Sunlight illuminating Discovery Rupes thrust fault scarp on Mercury, MESSENGER, 2011

better_than_last: Applies the scale_ladder structure by building from an assumed 1-to-1 tidal lock through Colombo's 59-day rotational measurement to the 176-day solar day reveal, while avoiding giveaway closing words to create an uninterrupted audio loop.
